audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart said "Skill" for Levels 1 through 6 while the content layer's win[0..4] and the packet levelChart both say Ahri. The page rendered two different answers to "who wins Level 1".
audit.why: Azir win rate is 47.17% over 1414 games and Ahri holds every lane stage before the first item: Orb of Deception is 970 range on a flat 7s cooldown against a soldier that must be summoned at 525 and attacks a short line, and Charm is 975 range on a flat 12s.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side moved to Ahri with matching ratings and rewritten whys; phases[5..6] stay Azir, matching content win[5..6].

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named Azir's ultimate "Shurima's Legacy" — that is his passive (Disc of the Sun from turret ruins). The wall is Emperor's Divide. It also asserted Ahri dashes through the wall, which the kits do not establish.
audit.why: Riot's text for Azir's passive is the turret Disc; Riot's text for R is the charging wall of soldiers. Spirit Rush is three casts with extra recasts on takedowns (Riot text), which is the real level-6 spike statement.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now names Emperor's Divide and states the verifiable recast rule instead of the wall-dash claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated anywhere on the page: Charm "instantly stops movement abilities", and Azir's E (Shifting Sands) is a dash. Charm cancels the shield-dash mid-flight.
audit.why: Riot's own Charm description says it instantly stops movement abilities; Azir's E is flagged dash and is his only escape at 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and content.mid.
sources: ownerKit E text and dash flag

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0] said Ahri can Charm you "through minions" / "through minion clutter".
audit.why: Riot's Charm text: it charms "an enemy it encounters" — it stops on the first thing it hits, so a minion body denies it. This is the single most actionable counterplay in the lane and the page taught the opposite.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to say Charm stops on the first unit it touches.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (catalogue defect 3), and dosFull[2].d called Charm a "fifteen-second" window; dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string pasted under an unrelated R title (catalogue defect 2).
audit.why: Charm is a flat 12s at every rank, Orb of Deception a flat 7s, Azir E 22s at rank 1, Spirit Rush 140/120/100, Emperor's Divide 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ahri was referred to as he/his/him across tldr, tradeGood, loading, phases[3].why, report[0], report[3], report[9], report[11], dosFull[0].t, dontsFull[1].t and breakdown.trading.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists ahri as female; the owner is addressed as "you", so every third-person pronoun refers to Ahri.
audit.corrected: All swapped to she/her at identical length.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentioned Grievous Wounds despite Essence Theft healing Ahri off minion waves and off takedowns.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule needs-antiheal for this exact matchup; Essence Theft heals after 9 minions and a larger amount on a takedown.
audit.corrected: breakdown.feeding now names Executioner's Calling timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet flagged whys[4] "Her Spirit Rush" as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: Spirit Rush is Ahri's real R name in the kit file. False positive — left alone.
